items.title: France snatch late winner in Belgium, Italy thrash Turkey 4-1 away
items.author: Mark Gleeson
items.creator: Mark Gleeson
items.summary: France substitute Michael Olise scored two minutes from time as the visitors snatched a late 1-0 win against Belgium in the Nations League on Monday, while Italy returned to winning ways with a thumping 4-1 away triumph over Turkey.
items.body:
France substitute Michael Olise scored two minutes from time as the visitors snatched a late 1-0 win against Belgium in the Nations League on Monday, while Italy returned to winning ways with a thumping 4-1 away triumph over Turkey.
Fortunes ebbed and flowed in Brussels but Olise kept up France coach Zinedine Zidane’s winning start to his new job with a surging run from midway inside the Belgian half before a superb finish to win the Group A1 fixture.
France were without captain Kylian Mbappe and Zidane made nine changes to the side that edged Turkey 1-0 last week but it was after bringing on the likes of Ousmane Dembele, Rayan Cherki and Olise that the French turned the game in their favour.
“We played a good game, we deserved to win, and we are all relieved by Michael’s goal," said France debutant Lucas da Cunha. "My performance? The coach gave me his full confidence and told me to express myself, to do what I do at club level. I felt good on the pitch."
Desire Doue was a persistent danger as he took on the home defence and twice hit the woodwork but Belgium will rue the opportunities they spurned with Mika Godts outstanding for them.
"It is a pity, especially because the goal came so late. We created chances ourselves, looked dangerous, and gave very little away. A draw would have been a fairer result," said Belgium centre back Brandon Mechele.
Italy lost last Friday’s opening fixture of their Nations League campaign 2-0 at home to Belgium in a false start for Roberto Mancini on his return to the coaching job, but in the rain in Bursa they looked a very different outfit.
Alessandro Bastoni gave the visitors a ninth-minute lead from a corner and 13 minutes later Davide Frattesi pounced on a rebound after Michael Kayode’s shot from the left was parried by goalkeeper Altay Bayındır.
Italy were 3-0 up in the 27th minute as debutant Kayode hit home a low effort and the visitors finished the half with 10 attempts such was their dominance.
FRENETIC GAME IN THE RAIN IN TURKEY The frenetic nature of the game continued after the break as Barıs Alper Yılmaz pulled one back for Turkey, who made three substitutions at halftime, but Italy’s three-goal advantage was restored as Pio Esposito headed home a fourth in the 50th.
"The team played well, pressed high, kept possession and played the ball through. We had to focus on this match, which was a difficult one," said Mancini, whose team go to Paris on Friday to face the French.
Bosnia registered an emphatic 4-2 win away to Romania in Bucharest in Group B4 as former great Gheorghe Hagi suffered another setback on his return to the manager's post.
But Sweden lead the group two points above Bosnia after a second home win, this time 3-1 over Poland in Stockholm.
The two Group B2 fixtures ended goalless with Ukraine away in Georgia and Northern Ireland home to Hungary.
Montenegro's Aleksa Latkovic scored a last-minute winner as they won 3-2 in Armenia to move three points clear of their opponents on six points atop Group C2 where Latvia and Cyprus drew 0-0 in Riga to each pick up their first point.

items.title: UK examines foreign state involvement in suspected airbase plot, releases suspects
items.author: CNA
items.summary: British police are investigating a suspected plot to attack RAF Fairford, a base used by US bombers, with five British men arrested and released on bail.
items.body:

UK examines foreign state involvement in suspected airbase plot, releases suspects

British police are investigating a suspected plot to attack RAF Fairford, a base used by US bombers, with five British men arrested and released on bail.

British newspaper front pages reporting the police declaration of a major incident at RAF Fairford airbase in this illustration, Sep 28, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Toby Melville)

FAIRFORD: British police said on Monday (Sep 28) they were investigating whether individuals acting for a foreign state were involved in an apparent plot to attack an airbase used by the United State s but said five suspects they had arrested would be released on bail.
The five men, all British nationals from London in their early 20s, were detained early on Sunday after police were alerted by a local farmer about three white vans driving towards RAF Fairford, a British base that houses US bombers that fly missions against Iran.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said in July the base was a legitimate target.
Laurence Taylor, who heads Britain's counter-terrorism police, said the men, who had been arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and planning a terrorist act, would be released under stringent bail conditions on Monday.

INVESTIGATION IS NOT OVER "To be very clear, this does not mean that the investigation is over," Taylor said in a state ment outside London police headquarters. "They absolutely remain under investigation as we explore multiple lines of enquiry."
US President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House on Monday that the incident "might be" connected to Iran, adding that he would not have released the suspects on bail. "I wouldn't have done that," he said.
A source familiar with the investigation had told Reuters that an Iranian-linked motive was considered the most likely, although a Russian sabotage operation or an Islamist plot were also being looked at as possibilities.
Iran's embassy in London had earlier said in a state ment it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns the recent unfounded and malicious speculations" that it was involved, which it said would fuel "Iranophobia propaganda" in Britain.
Taylor, who did not specifically refer to Iran, said he knew there was significant interest in whether the current geopolitical context had a bearing on this incident.
"Be assured, we are considering this from every possible angle, including that this may be actively committed by proxies or individuals either knowingly or unknowingly working on behalf of a foreign state ."

Armed police officers work on a road outside the perimeter of the RAF Fairford airbase, Gloucestershire, Britain, Sep 27, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Toby Shepheard)

POLICE REMAIN AT SCENE Taylor said the three white vans had been subject to extensive examination, with the support of the military and forensic experts, and police still had "significant resources deployed at the scene".
Trump said on Sunday that the suspects had been looking to do "big damage" and had been under investigation by British and US authorities. However, doubts were voiced in British media about the degree to which they had been under surveillance, given how close they had come to the base.
The source familiar with the investigation said the arrests were not "intelligence-led", although security had been heightened at the base, suggesting authorities were aware of an increased threat.
The farmer who alerted the police told reporters she had seen a group of "hooded and masked men" running into fields. The farmer, who has not been identified, said she believed it was her phone call to the 999 emergency hotline that foiled any plot and that she thought she had seen up to 10 people at the scene.
Defence minister Wes Streeting told the BBC the farmer had only a "partial picture" of the investigation, without providing further clarification.
"We know that Iran and their proxies wish to do us harm. We know that they hate our democracy, and we know that we regularly have to thwart Iranian attempts to threaten either our interests or indeed our allies," Streeting said.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham chaired a meeting of the government's emergency response committee.

TERRORISM THREAT SEVERE Britain raised its national terrorism threat level to its second highest level in April after a series of antisemitic incidents in north London, meaning an attack is considered highly likely.
Police said they were investigating links with Iran to many of those incidents in which properties connected to the Jewish community or Iranian dissidents were targeted.
After the Fairford arrests, the US embassy issued a security alert saying US citizens should exercise caution and be "mindful of personal security". Security was stepped up at other US airbase s in Britain.
The British government had given authorisation to the US to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
In Fairford, police imposed a 400-metre cordon around the base and evacuated residents from 85 homes in the nearby village of Whelford.
"Thanks to the excellent work of the army's explosive ordnance disposal team, the scene is now safe, and the residents of Whelford will shortly be returning home," British interior minister Shabana Mahmood said.

Source: Reuters/fs

items.title: UAE president discussed bilateral relations with Israel's Netanyahu, state news agency says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan discussed bilateral relations during a visit on Sunday by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to the Gulf country, the Emirati state news agency WAM reported on Monday.
items.body:
UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan discussed bilateral relations during a [USN:S8N40N018 TEXT:"visit"] on Sunday by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to the Gulf country, the Emirati state news agency WAM reported on Monday.
The report by WAM was the first UAE confirmation of Netanyahu's visit.
The Israeli prime minister's office said on Monday that Netanyahu visited at the invitation of the UAE president. It said the visit "focused on strengthening relations between the two countries and on regional challenges".
Three senior Israeli officials said the meeting on Sunday lasted six hours and focused on Iran.
Earlier this year, the UAE [USN:S8N40H01C TEXT:"denied"] that Sheikh Mohamed met with Netanyahu after the Israeli prime minister's office said in May that Netanyahu had "secretly visited" the Gulf country and met with the president.
A source familiar with the meeting said at the time that Netanyahu and Sheikh Mohamed met in Al-Ain, an oasis city in Abu Dhabi along the country's border with Oman, on March 26.
Since coming under attack during the Iran war, the UAE has strengthened its relationships with the United States and Israel, with which it opened ties as a result of the 2020 Abraham Accords. The relationship with Israel gives the UAE a lever for regional influence and a unique channel to Washington.

items.title: Trading Day: Blue Monday
items.author: Jamie McGeever
items.creator: Jamie McGeever
items.summary: The global bond slump accelerated on Monday, pushing yields to new, multi-decade highs, as oil prices rallied after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace proposal from Iran. Stock markets duly fell, although news that the two sides are set to hold separate talks with mediators eased the selling pressure across asset classes.
items.body:
The global bond slump accelerated on Monday, pushing yields to new, multi-decade highs, as oil prices rallied after US President Donald Trump [USN:L6N45I003 TEXT:"rejected"] a peace proposal from Iran. [USN:L6N45K0GS TEXT:"Stock markets"] duly fell, although news that the two sides are set to hold separate talks with [USN:S8N42G02R TEXT:"mediators"] eased the selling pressure across asset classes.
In [USN:L6N45H0VH TEXT:"my column today"], I examine whether the US can grow its way out of its debt crisis. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is hoping AI-driven growth and productivity will save the day, but a repeat of the 1990s, when the internet boom boosted tax receipts and shrank the deficit, is unlikely.
Today's Key Reads
[USN:L6N45K0LY TEXT:"Nvidia boosts share buyback by record $150 billion as AI boom fuels growth"]
[USN:P8N42O09S TEXT:"China, US agree to tariff cuts on $60 billion of goods including agriculture, household items"]
[USN:P8N44H01V TEXT:"China's industrial profit growth slows further as economic imbalances deepen"]
[USN:L6N44114G TEXT:"Prediction markets' push into US stocks raises regulatory alarm bells"]
[USN:L1N45K0A4 TEXT:"The political chess behind the ECB's next leadership shake-up"]
Today's Key Market Moves
STOCKS: South Korea -2.7%, China -2% to lowest since Aug last year. [USN:L6N45K0DO TEXT:"Europe"] and [USN:L6N45K0HC TEXT:"UK"] little-changed. Dow -0.7%, S&P 500 -0.8%, Nasdaq -0.9%.
SECTORS/SHARES: Eight sectors on the S&P 500 fall, three rise. Comms services -1.7%, consumer staples +0.4%. [USN:L1N45K0OS TEXT:"Boeing"] -7%, Qualcomm -7%, Intel -6%. Palo Alto Networks +5%, Paramount [USN:L4N45H17Y TEXT:"Skydance"] +3%.
FX: Dollar edges up. [USN:L6N45K110 TEXT:"Colombian"] peso -2.5%, Mexican peso -2%.
BONDS: The selloff continues. French, German, UK, US benchmark 10-year yields all highest since mid-late 2000s. US curves eventually end a touch flatter.
COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L4N45J03L TEXT:"Oil"] rises, Brent +1%. [USN:L4N45K00C TEXT:"Gold"] -3.5% to 7-week low.

Today's Talking Points:
AI debt cracks appear
US corporate debt markets have been remarkably resilient in the face of soaring Treasury yields and growing concern over AI data center buildout costs. Until now. Cracks are beginning to appear — high-yield spreads broke out on Friday to the widest since April and are approaching 300 basis points, but investment-grade spreads are finally starting to move too. They ended last week at 81 bps, and on Monday likely hit the widest since April.
Oracle's debt issues are nothing new, but the blowout in the company's borrowing costs and CDS rates is still remarkable. Meta's bond yields and CDS are also breaking sharply higher. Hyperscalers' bond issuance this year is around $220 billion, and could double next year. It will come at a price, though. An increasingly high price.
Another Nvidia record
[USN:L6N45K0LY TEXT:"Nvidia"], the world's most valuable company, is boosting its share buyback authorization by a record $150 billion. This brings its remaining buyback capacity to $235 billion, which it expects to deploy through fiscal 2028. It's an extraordinary amount of share-price-boosting firepower, even for a $5.5 trillion market cap entity.
Shares bucked the downbeat market on Monday, rising nearly 2%. The buyback move suggests Nvidia thinks its share price should be higher. It's a vote of confidence in the business from the top. As ever with buybacks, however, there's always the nagging doubt that they show a lack of better alternatives.
The cold rush
Investors are cooling on [USN:L8N45K1C9 TEXT:"gold"]. The yellow metal fell to its lowest in nearly two months on Monday, its 3.5% fall the steepest since early June. Is a break back below $4,000/oz on the cards? It wouldn't be a surprise - the dollar is rising, the Fed seems to be at the beginning of a tightening cycle, and Treasury yields are soaring. None of that is gold-friendly, and US-Iran detente would also dim gold's safe-haven allure.
But central banks are sure to be big buyers on dips, if their behavior in recent years is any guide. They have steadily added gold to their reserves, and major holder China is leading the way — Beijing bought 650,000 ounces, nearly 20 tons, in August, the most since October 2023.

items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Iran's Qeshm Island had not come under strike and no explosions were reported there, state TV said on Monday, citing local sources, after state news agency IRNA said an explosion-like sound had been heard from the direction of the sea.
items.body:
Iran's Qeshm Island had not come under strike and no explosions were reported there, state TV said on Monday, citing local sources, after state news agency IRNA said an explosion-like sound had been heard from the direction of the sea.
The sources told state TV the sound was similar to those heard on previous nights and was usually linked to warning shots fired at vessels violating waterway regulations.
There was no immediate independent confirmation of the cause of the sound.

items.title: Pope Leo defends entering political fray on France end-of-life law
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Pope Leo on Monday defended his decision to vocally oppose assisted dying initiatives while in France, acknowledging he may have entered the political fray two months after the country approved such a measure, but wanted to share the Catholic Church's viewpoint.
items.body:
Pope Leo on Monday defended his decision to vocally oppose assisted dying initiatives while in France, acknowledging he may have entered the political fray two months after the country approved such a measure, but wanted to share the Catholic Church's viewpoint.
"If that's politics, I did that, but it was not to get involved in French politics, it was to teach what the Church really believes," the first US pope told journalists on his flight back to Rome from his four-day visit to France.
Leo criticized assisted-dying measures several times during his three-city tour. On Sunday he told healthcare workers in Lourdes, France that their job is "to care for a suffering person, not to eliminate that person."
France's new law, which created a legal right to die for those with incurable illnesses after years of intense debate, drew heated opposition from local Catholic bishops.
Leo said on Monday he did not think he crossed any lines between Church and state.
"When I went to France, I went primarily to preach the Gospel," he said.
The Catholic Church teaches that all human life is sacred and opposes abortion, assisted dying and the death penalty.

items.body:
[ローマ教皇専用機中　２８日　ロイター] - ローマ教皇レオ１４世は２８日、ロシアとウクライナに対し、４年に及ぶ戦争を終わらせる方法について話し合うよう呼びかけた。

教皇は、４日間のフランス訪問を終えてローマに戻る機中で記者団に応じ、一部の各国指導者が「核兵器や、ますます破壊的になりつつある戦争について語り始めている」と非難。その上で、「教会には、ロシアとウクライナ、そして他の国々の指導者に、共に集まり、対話の席に着くよう絶えず呼びかける責任がある」と語った。

また、指導者たちは「もはや意味をなさないこれらの戦争を継続することなく、問題を解決する方法を模索しなければならない」と述べた。

これに先立ち教皇は、フランス東部メスで演説。欧州の指導者らに対し、「戦争は欧州にまで戻ってきた。新たな無意味な殺りくが、毎日数え切れないほどの民間人の命を奪っている」と述べ、紛争の終結や平和の実現に向けて自らの立場や主張の一部を譲歩する姿勢を持つよう訴えた。

また、欧州の軍事費増加に対する反対姿勢を改めて示し、「再軍備が答えだという幻想にも警戒しなければならない」と述べた。

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump's meeting with tech CEOs on artificial intelligence on Tuesday (Sep 28) will focus on finding a balance between innovation and oversight, Ho us e Speaker Mike Johnson s ai d, as the federal government seeks to define its role in the burgeoning tech nology.
"We do not need a moratorium. We do not need to jump in and hyper-regulate this, beca us e we'll lose the race to China," Johnson s ai d in an interview on Monday with Fox B us iness Network. "The innovation is important to continue, but we have to strike the right balance . That's what the conversation is going to be about."
Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, Anthropic's Dario Amodei, Open AI 's Greg Brockman and Nvidia's Jensen Huang are among those who will attend Tuesday's meeting with Trump and Johnson, according to sources familiar with the matter. Other possible attendees include Google CEO Sundar Pich ai and Spacex AI executive Elon M us k.
The White Ho us e meeting comes as leading AI companies are calling for slowing development of increasingly capable AI systems , warning of the risks to humanity and appealing for governments to work together to manage the increasingly powerful tech nology.

Trump has downplayed concerns over the mis us e of artificial intelligence harming people as he stressed the importance of maintaining America's competitive edge over China. He says the US already has guardr ai ls in place for the powerful tech nology, including at the Department of J us tice.
Johnson s ai d the US should be mindful of safety but not stymie the tech nology's development. "I think there may be a role for the DOJ if things go awry. But what we need before we get to that stage is transparency, and we need some oversight," he s ai d on "Mornings with Fox B us iness."
Lawmakers in both parties have questioned Trump's hands-off approach even as the tech nology r ai ses fears about safety, job losses and the concentration of power among a handful of tech companies.
Ho us e Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries s ai d AI ind us try leaders were pleading for some government action and Congress has a responsibility to protect the American people.
"So, when it comes to AI safety, it cert ai nly seems to me that we need to actually lean in boldly and responsibly - now," Jeffries told CNBC on Monday.
The president had dinner with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Sunday.
Anthropic and its rivals have called for slowing AI development. These include Open AI , Google’s DeepMind, Microsoft and x AI .

items.title: AMD adquirirá World Labs de la científica Fei-Fei Li en operación de 8.200 millones de dólares
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices anunció el lunes que había llegado a un acuerdo para adquirir la empresa emergente World Labs, fundada por la pionera de la inteligenca artificial Fei-Fei Li, en un negocio valorado en 8.200 millones de dólares.
items.body:
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) anunció el lunes que había llegado a un acuerdo para adquirir la empresa emergente World Labs, fundada por la pionera de la inteligenca artificial Fei-Fei Li, en un negocio valorado en 8.200 millones de dólares.
World Labs, de San Francisco, que recaudó 1.000 millones de dólares en una ronda de financiación este año, desarrolla modelos de inteligencia espacial.
La inteligencia espacial, un enfoque novedoso de la IA, se refiere a la capacidad de razonar cómo funciona el mundo en 3D, en lugar de basarse en datos en 2D, como imágenes planas o texto.
Fei-Fei Li se incorporará a AMD como vicepresidenta ejecutiva y directora científica. Dependerá directamente de la presidenta ejecutiva Lisa Su.
Se espera que la operación se cierre a finales de 2026.

items.title: Monedas bajan ante punto muerto EEUU-Irán y expectativas alza tasas Fed
items.author: Froilan Romero
items.creator: Froilan Romero
items.summary: Las principales monedas de América Latina bajaron el lunes, en medio de un aumento en los precios del petróleo por la tensión entre Estados Unidos e irán que avivaba los temores inflacionarios, lo que reforzaba las expectativas de una nueva alza en las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos.
items.body:
Las principales monedas de América Latina bajaron el lunes, en medio de un aumento en los precios del petróleo por la tensión entre Estados Unidos e irán que avivaba los temores inflacionarios, lo que reforzaba las expectativas de una nueva alza en las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos.
* [USN:L6N45K10E TEXT:"Los precios del petróleo"] subieron el lunes, pero retrocedieron desde máximos de la sesión por las expectativas de que los mediadores de Qatar mantengan conversaciones con Estados Unidos e Irán para intentar alcanzar un posible acuerdo de paz.
* En las primeras horas de la sesión, los precios se dispararon más de 4 dólares por barril después de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, rechazó una propuesta de Irán que habría permitido reabrir el estrecho de Ormuz.
* [USN:L6N45K0RK TEXT:"Los mediadores qataríes"] tienen previsto mantener conversaciones por separado con el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores iraní, Abás Araqchi, en Nueva York, y con la parte estadounidense el lunes o el martes, dijo a Reuters un funcionario al tanto de las negociaciones.
* Trump dijo el lunes que funcionarios de su Gobierno mantuvieron conversaciones con los mediadores que intentan poner fin a la guerra con Irán, y añadió que Estados Unidos ganará el conflicto "muy pronto".
* Los operadores ven un 70,3% de probabilidades de que la Fed suba las tasas en octubre, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME. El banco central estadounidense aumentó los tipos este mes en un cuarto de punto porcentual e indicó que es probable que haya nuevas alzas.
* Por su parte, el índice dólar , que compara a la divisa estadounidense frente a una canasta de seis grandes monedas, operaba prácticamente estable aunque cerca de un máximo de dos meses.
* El peso mexicano cotizaba cerca del cierre en 17,9737 por dólar, con una caída del 1,73% por el fortalecimiento global del dólar, al inicio de una semana marcada por una serie de datos laborales de Estados Unidos, incluida la nómina no agrícola del viernes, clave para las perspectivas de la Reserva Federal tras su alza de este mes.
* El Banco de México, en cambio, mantuvo su tasa clave sin cambios la semana pasada y señaló que no replicará automáticamente las decisiones de la Fed, profundizando recientes presiones sobre el peso, que había iniciado el mes en 16,8520 unidades, su mejor nivel desde mayo de 2024.
* El principal índice accionario S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , que integran las 35 empresas más líquidas del mercado mexicano, caía un 0,08%, a 64.950,42 unidades, por la aversión global al riesgo y en línea con un débil desempeño de Wall Street.
* El real brasileño se depreció un 0,83%, a 5,2264 unidades por dólar, para anotar un mínimo en seis meses; mientras que el índice Bovespa (.BVSP) de la bolsa B3 de Sao Paulo retrocedió un 0,21%, a 183.089,66 puntos, según las cifras preliminares de cierre.
* Los inversores también analizaban a sondeos antes de las elecciones presidenciales del fin de semana. Dos encuestas arrojaron que el presidente de izquierda Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva y el candidato de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro se encuentran en un virtual empate de cara a la segunda ronda, ya que se espera que ningún postulante logre la ventaja necesaria en la primera ronda.
* En Argentina, el peso mayorista cerró estable en 1.525 por dólar , tras anotar su piso récord intradiario en 1.535 unidades. En tanto, el índice bursátil Merval (.MERV) cayó un 3,28% y arrastró su séptima baja consecutiva con un descenso acumulado del 8,58%.
* El Gobierno viene de reportar una fuerte caída en el consumo y un aumento en los niveles de la pobreza, lo que alienta temores de una recesión a un año de cruciales elecciones presidenciales.
* El peso chileno , bajó un 0,37%, a 964,80/965,10 unidades, su menor valor de cierre en más de un año, presionado también por una caída en los precios del cobre, el mayor envío del país. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , cedió un 1,06%, a 11.137,23 unidades.
* Los precios del cobre tocaron el lunes su nivel más bajo en más de una semana, ya que los datos económicos desfavorables de China —el principal consumidor—, el aumento de los precios del petróleo y la apreciación del dólar reforzaban las perspectivas de una demanda débil.
* El peso colombiano cerró con caída de un 1,51% a 3.362 unidades por dólar, tras la efímera recuperación de la sesión anterior y retomando la depreciación derivada en parte de las preocupaciones fiscales sobre el país andino; al tiempo que el índice accionario MSCI COLCAP (.COLCAP) retrocedió un 0,21% a 2.579,33 puntos.
* El domingo en la noche el presidente colombiano Abelardo De La Espriella informó que dio instrucciones al equipo económico para que sostenga conversaciones con el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) para buscar una salida a la crisis fiscal que enfrenta el país.
* "La lectura inicial de los mercados parece ser negativa, pues deja en evidencia la vulnerable situación de liquidez que enfrenta la Nación y los fuertes retos para que el ajuste fiscal provenga de recortes de gasto profundos", escribió el Banco de Bogotá.
* La moneda peruana, el sol , cayó un 0,52%, a 3.4390/3.4420 unidades por dólar. Por otra parte, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) bajó un 0,79%, a 1.585 puntos.

items.title: Maxhosa Africa brings pan-Africanism to Paris Fashion Week
items.author: Helen Reid
items.creator: Helen Reid
items.summary: Maxhosa Africa creative director Laduma Ngxokolo unveiled a collection that celebrated pan-Africanism on Monday, as his label became the first South African brand to stage a full runway show on the official Paris Fashion Week calendar.
items.body:
Maxhosa Africa creative director Laduma Ngxokolo unveiled a collection that celebrated pan-Africanism on Monday, as his label became the first South African brand to stage a full runway show on the official Paris Fashion Week calendar.
Ngxokolo said he wanted the show to highlight South Africa's diversity, beauty, and business successes.
"That's the Africa that we all want to live in, where the economy thrives, where the crimes become less, where politically it's less corrupt — that's the Africa that we're trying to showcase here," Ngxokolo told journalists after the show in the gilded rooms of the residence of the South African ambassador to France.
Maxhosa Africa clothes are produced at two knitting factories the brand owns in Johannesburg and in East London, in the Eastern Cape province where the wool used for its knitwear is also sourced. Ngxokolo said he aims to boost the country's textile industry and show it can produce high-quality luxury goods.
On a catwalk of woven straw mats models paraded outfits that echoed the pan-African theme. One featured multi-coloured knitted labels with the names of African countries, a motif also worn by South African musician and rapper Sjava, whose singing provided the soundtrack to the show.
Women wore brightly patterned bra tops with wavy hems, paired with flowing midi skirts, or matching geometric-patterned knit ensembles of pleated skirts and button-down shirts in lilac and grey. Some sported glasses by Kenyan artist Cyrus Kabiru, who creates eyewear from waste.
Menswear ranged from the formal, like a blue and red double-breasted suit in a checkerboard knit covered in beaded symbols, to more casual streetwear looks of baggy shorts and polo shirts in bright diamond patterns.
While Maxhosa's geometric patterns evoke traditional Xhosa beadwork, Ngxokolo said his inspirations also included Missoni, Gucci, and Louis Vuitton.
Ngxokolo had been planning to bring other African designers to Paris with him, but said he didn't have the resources.
"I feel honoured to be represented, I've been fighting to sit at the table for 16 years now," he said. "We feel that we are still underrepresented as the African continent."

items.title: Cook, do Fed, prevê mais pressões inflacionárias à frente
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A diretora do Federal Reserve Lisa Cook afirmou nesta segunda-feira que espera que as pressões inflacionárias continuem nos próximos meses, decorrentes da demanda relacionada à IA e dos preços mais altos do petróleo, embora não tenha chegado a afirmar que serão necessários novos aumentos nas taxas de juros.
items.body:
A diretora do Federal Reserve Lisa Cook afirmou nesta segunda-feira que espera que as pressões inflacionárias continuem nos próximos meses, decorrentes da demanda relacionada à IA e dos preços mais altos do petróleo, embora não tenha chegado a afirmar que serão necessários novos aumentos nas taxas de juros.
“O mercado de trabalho parece estar bem posicionado para lidar com um aumento das taxas”, disse Cook em declarações preparadas para divulgação em uma conferência sobre IA e tecnologias emergentes em Oakland, na Califórnia. “Olhando à frente, vou considerar qual taxa de juros de referência pode ser necessária para continuar a conduzir a inflação de volta à nossa meta. É claro que o número e a magnitude de quaisquer ajustes futuros serão determinados pelas observações da reação da economia às nossas medidas de política monetária até o momento e pelos dados de inflação e do mercado de trabalho nos próximos meses.”
O Fed elevou sua taxa de juros este mês pela primeira vez em três anos para ajudar a trazer a inflação de volta à meta de 2% do banco central dos EUA de maneira tempestiva. Cook participou da votação unânime em apoio à decisão.
Os formuladores de política monetária do Fed previram mais um aumento da taxa até o final deste ano para lidar com a inflação, que está acima da meta de 2% há mais de cinco anos e vem sendo impulsionada para cima pelo aumento dos preços globais da energia durante a guerra dos EUA e Israel contra o Irã, que já dura sete meses.
Os preços do petróleo subiram cerca de 2% nesta segunda-feira, depois que o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, rejeitou um acordo do Irã para reabrir o Estreito de Ormuz. Os mercados financeiros estão agora precificando uma chance de cerca de 75% de um aumento da taxa pelo Fed no próximo mês e uma forte probabilidade de um terceiro aumento consecutivo na reunião de dezembro.
Cook não confirmou essas expectativas em seu discurso preparado, embora tenha observado que a inflação tem estado “alta demais por tempo demais” e que a inflação total ficou em cerca de 3,8% nos 12 meses até agosto, praticamente o dobro da meta de 2%.
“Além disso, nos próximos meses, espero ver pressão contínua sobre a inflação decorrente da expansão da IA, conforme discutido hoje, e do repasse dos preços mais altos do petróleo e das interrupções na cadeia de abastecimento associadas ao conflito no Oriente Médio”, disse ela.
Embora ela espere que os ganhos de produtividade impulsionados pela IA tragam alguma desinflação no médio prazo, Cook disse que esses ganhos não ocorrerão com rapidez suficiente para compensar as pressões inflacionárias neste ano. Os dados sobre a inflação mostram que esses efeitos estão se espalhando para além dos setores focados em IA, afirmou ela.
As falas de Cook concentraram-se principalmente nos efeitos econômicos da IA, que ela vê como uma tecnologia de uso geral com potencial transformador para a economia.
Até o momento, ela disse ver poucas evidências de que a IA esteja remodelando a estrutura do mercado de trabalho, mas acrescentou que está “muito atenta” à possibilidade de que ela possa elevar a taxa de desemprego, pelo menos temporariamente — uma situação que o Fed teria margem limitada para combater, pois um corte nas taxas destinado a ajudar o mercado de trabalho poderia alimentar a inflação.

items.title: Trump Spurns Iran's Latest Offer; Former Disney CEO Bob Chapek
items.summary: The selloff in the US bond market deepened on Monday after President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, dampening hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough to end the war. We get reaction from Bloomberg's Ira Jersey. Iranian officials have privately expressed pessimism about reaching a deal to end hostilities with Washington and reopen the Strait of Hormuz before US midterm elections in November, according to people familiar with the matter. Iran and the US made little progress during talks in New York on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly last week and the Islamic Republic believes there’s a high chance of the conflict escalating after the November 3rd vote. We speak with former Under Secretary of the US Army, Patrick Murphy. Plus - former Disney CEO Bob Chapek joins for an extended conversation on his book 'Behind the Castle Walls.' (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Trader Joe's didn't mismanage forfeited funds in retirement plan, US judge rules
items.author: Daniel Wiessner
items.creator: Daniel Wiessner
items.summary: A federal judge in Boston ruled on Monday that Trader Joe's did not violate the federal law regulating employee benefits by using forfeited worker contributions to offset its own payments to an employee retirement plan.
items.body:
A federal judge in Boston ruled on Monday that Trader Joe's did not violate the federal law regulating employee benefits by using forfeited worker contributions to offset its own payments to an employee retirement plan.
Dozens of companies [USN:L1N3NW0AY TEXT:"including Amazon.com"], Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase and Northrop Grumman have faced similar claims in recent years, and the Trader Joe's case in May became the first to go to trial
The class action on behalf of more than 40,000 plan participants was filed last year
During the six-day bench trial, US District Judge William Young dismissed claims that Trader Joe's improperly used forfeited funds for its own benefit
Young on Monday said the money went back into the retirement plan, benefiting participants
The plaintiffs prevailed on a claim that Trader Joe's failed to take steps to minimize recordkeeping fees
Young awarded about $1.2 million in damages and interest, far below the more than $9 million sought in the lawsuit
The case is Stephan v. Trader Joe's Company, US District Court for the District of Massachusetts, No. 1:25-cv-10212.
For the plaintiffs: James Maro, James Wells and Mark Gyandoh of Capozzi Adler; Peter Muhic of Muhic Law
For Trader Joe's: Catalina Vergara, Deanna Rice and others from O'Melveny & Myers
Read more:
[USN:L1N3NW0AY TEXT:"Amazon accused in lawsuit of mismanaging forfeited 401(k) funds"]

items.title: Bond yields crank higher and pull U.S. stocks further from their record
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: Surging crude prices are dragging on U.S. futures after President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
items.body: NEW YORK — Yields in the U.S. bond market cranked higher Monday and again touched their highest levels in roughly two decades, which knocked U.S. stocks further from their record high. The S&P 500 fell 0.8 per cent and gave back much of its gain from last week, which had brought it to the brink of its all-time high. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 347 points, or 0.7 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite sank 0.9 per cent. Stocks felt pressure as the yield on the 10-year Treasury briefly topped 5.27 per cent before pulling back to 5.23 per cent, up from 5.17 per cent late Friday. It’s back to where it was in 2007, before the financial crisis and Great Recession sent yields toward zero. The 30-year Treasury yield rose to 5.55 per cent from 5.49 per cent and is back to where it was in 2004. Treasury yields have been rising for a range of reasons, from worries about inflation to Washington’s massive debt load to signs that the U.S. economy remains solid despite its many challenges. That pressures the economy because higher yields make borrowing money more expensive for everyone, while also undercutting prices for stocks and other investments. Monday’s rise in yields followed the latest swings for oil prices, which have been yo-yoing on uncertainty about when the war with Iran will allow tankers to flow freely again through the Strait of Hormuz. That would allow them deliver oil from the Middle East to customers worldwide. The latest turns came after President Donald Trump said over the weekend he’s rejecting an offer from Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume talks on its nuclear program. “I’d like to make a deal, too,” Trump said Saturday. “But that deal would not be acceptable.” The price for Brent crude in the most actively traded part of the oil market briefly climbed above US$101 per barrel Monday morning, but it pared its gains as U.S. officials said mediators were still working with Iran and the United States on a deal to end the fighting and open the strait. It settled at US$97.83, up 0.4 per cent. For all its ups and downs, a barrel of Brent remains much more expensive than the roughly US$72 it cost before the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February. That has helped worsen inflation, and the average price for a gallon of regular gasoline is up to nearly US$4.48 from US$3.13 a year ago, according to AAA. On Wall Street, stocks of airlines and other companies with big fuel bills sank because of the rise in oil prices. American Airlines fell 2.5 per cent, and United Airlines lost 2.2 per cent. Gold miners were also weak after the price of gold sank 3.5 per cent. Gold has a reputation for helping to protect its investors from high inflation, but its price tends to weaken when rising yields mean bonds are paying investors more in interest. Gold struggles to keep up because it pays its investors nothing. Newmont, the Denver-based mining giant, slid 4.4 per cent. One of Wall Street’s bigger losses hit MongoDB, which dropped 18.5 per cent after the database company said its CEO, Chirantan “CJ” Desai, is stepping down immediately to pursue a senior role at Meta Platforms. Such losses more than offset a 1.7 per cent rise for Nvidia, Wall Street’s most influential stock. The chip company’s stock climbed after it said its board approved a plan to send up to another US$150 billion to its shareholders in a stock buyback plan, bringing the program’s total remaining size to US$235 billion. Nvidia has the power to do so after the frenzy around its chips used for artificial-intelligence technology helped it more than double the amount of cash on its books in the first half of its fiscal year. The company also on Monday unveiled a new security platform that the chipmaker said can stop artificial intelligence agents from going rogue. AI stocks have broadly come under pressure after leaders of the industry said it needs to slow its development to give safety measures time to catch up. All told, the S&P 500 fell 59.72 points to 7,683.69. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 347.11 to 51,481.51, and the Nasdaq composite sank 248.34 to 26,820.38. In stock markets abroad, European indexes were mixed following weaker performances across much of Asia. Indexes dropped 2.7 per cent in Seoul and 1.7 per cent in Shanghai for two of the world’s bigger moves. ___ Stan Choe, The Associated Press AP Business Writers Yuri Kageyama and Michelle Chapman contributed to this report.

items.title: Incêndio em imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida não tem relação com apoiadores de Flávio
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Um vídeo de uma imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida pegando fogo não é deste mês nem tem relação com apoiadores do senador Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato à Presidência pelo PL, como afirmam publicações nas redes sociais.
items.body:
Um vídeo de uma imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida pegando fogo não é deste mês nem tem relação com apoiadores do senador Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato à Presidência pelo PL, como afirmam publicações nas redes sociais.
Estes são os principais detalhes:
“Bolsonaristas na noite de ontem começaram a atacar as igrejas de Nossa Senhora Aparecida. As investigações estão em andamento, um suspeito foi preso e estava com adesivo de campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro”, dizem postagens no Facebook e no Instagram com a gravação.
No entanto, o registro é de julho e mostra um incêndio em uma estátua da santa em Nerópolis (GO), como noticiado por veículos de imprensa como a TV Anhanguera , afiliada da TV Globo em Goiás, e o UOL .
Um vídeo publicado pela Prefeitura de Nerópolis no Facebook em julho mostra o local do incêndio e permite identificar o mesmo cenário visto no conteúdo checado.
Procurada, a Polícia Civil não respondeu de imediato. Na época, o delegado André Fernandes disse à TV Anhanguera que o incidente foi causado por velas colocadas por fiéis e excluiu hipóteses de intolerância religiosa ou vandalismo.
Na semana passada, Flávio Bolsonaro negou um rumor de que retiraria de Nossa Senhora Aparecida o título de padroeira do Brasil caso eleito.
Veredicto: Legenda errada. O vídeo do incêndio de uma imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida em Nerópolis (GO) é de julho e foi acidental, segundo a Polícia Civil.
Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

items.title: 米国株式市場＝反落、ダウ347ドル安　原油高や米債利回り上昇が重し
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ニューヨーク　２８日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ニューヨーク　２８日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は反落。原油価格と米債利回りの上昇が相場の重しとなった。投資家は、米国とイランの和平合意を巡る不確実性や、それに伴う米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の金利の道筋への影響を見極めようとしている。

Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種の下落率は８月２０日以来の大きさとなった。

原油価格は、トランプ米大統領がイランの和平案を拒否したことを受けて上昇した。ただ、仲介国カタールが合意の可能性を探るため両国と協議するとの期待から、上げ幅を縮小した。

米国債利回りは原油と軽油の値上がりを背景としたインフレ懸念に加え、追加利上げの可能性を示唆するＦＲＢ当局者の発言を受けて上昇している。 

クレセット・キャピタル・マネジメントの最高投資ストラテジスト兼創業パートナー、ジャック・アブリン氏は「イラン情勢が原油価格を押し上げ、原油価格がインフレを押し上げ、インフレが金利を押し上げている」と指摘。「金利水準からみて、債券が株式に比べてかなり魅力的に映る局面に入りつつある。これは約２０年ぶりのことで、注目すべき状況だ」と述べた。また「今は企業収益よりもバリュエーションが焦点になっている」と語った。

個別銘柄ではボーイングが６．９％急落し、ダウの主な押し下げ要因の一つとなった。米連邦航空局（ＦＡＡ）が、新たに判明したソフトウエアの問題が解決するまで「７３７ＭＡＸ１０」の認証を遅らせると発表したことを嫌気した。

一方、半導体大手エヌビディアは相場全体に逆行して１．６％上昇。自社株買い枠を１５００億ドル拡大したことが材料視された。

テスラは３．９％安。ＪＰモルガンが第３・四半期の納車台数の低迷を理由に目標株価を引き下げた。

ＦＲＢのクック理事は２８日、人工知能（ＡＩ）関連の需要と原油高を背景に、今後数カ月はインフレ圧力が続くとの見通しを示した。ただ、追加利上げが必要になるとの明言は避けた。

経済が堅調なペースで成長していることを示す経済指標などを背景に、ＦＲＢが１０月の会合で利上げするとの観測がここ数日で強まっている。ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、市場は現在、同会合で少なくとも２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の利上げが行われる確率を７０．３％織り込み、１週間前の５７．６％から上昇している。

今週はＦＲＢの政策の方向性を左右し得る重要経済指標の発表が相次ぐ。物価や労働市場に関する指標が予定され、１０月２日には雇用統計が発表される。

ニューヨーク証券取引所では値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を３．５５対１の比率で上回った。ナスダックでも２．５６対１で値下がり銘柄が多かった。

米取引所の合算出来高は１６７億１０００万株。直近２０営業日の平均は１６８億５０００万株。

items.title: Tesoro argentino adjudica equivalente a 5.850 mln dlr en licitación de títulos
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Argentina colocó títulos del Tesoro por un valor efectivo de 8,62 billones de pesos (unos 5.850 millones de dólares) en una licitación doméstica de distintos instrumentos para refinanciar vencimientos, informó el lunes la Secretaría de Finanzas.
items.body:
Argentina colocó títulos del Tesoro por un valor efectivo de 8,62 billones de pesos (unos 5.850 millones de dólares) en una licitación doméstica de distintos instrumentos para refinanciar vencimientos, informó el lunes la Secretaría de Finanzas.
La licitación, por la que se recibió un total de ofertas por 9,77 billones de pesos, abarcó una renovación ("rollover") del 100,08% de los vencimientos previstos.
El Tesoro buscó renovar originalmente unos 8,1 billones de pesos en vencimientos de deuda interna.
El menú ofertado consistió en una letra "Lecap" corta (S13N6), una "Lecer" (X29E7), dos "Bontam" (TMF27 y TML27) y cuatro "dollar linked" (D30O6, D30N6, D31M7 y TZV27). Como sucedió en agosto, el Tesoro no puso a disposición papeles con vencimiento en el próximo mandato presidencial, desde diciembre de 2027.
(1 dólar = 1.525 pesos )

items.title: ＵＡＥ副大統領が29日サウジ訪問、国防相が招待＝国営通信
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [２８日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[２８日 ロイター] - サウジアラビアのハリド・ビン・サルマン国防相は、アラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）のマンスール・ビン・ザイド副大統領兼副首相を２９日にサウジ訪問に招待した。サウジ国営メディアが２８日、報じた。

ＵＡＥの国営通信ＷＡＭは、マンスール氏は招待を受け、サウジを訪問すると報じている。ただ、詳細は伝えていない。

サウジを巡っては、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派がミサイルやドローン（無人機）による攻撃を繰り返している。サウジはフーシ派への対応を巡り国際的な支持の取り付けを進めているが、協力の要請がＵＡＥにも及んでいるかは現時点で分かっていない。

ＵＡＥのＷＡＭはこの日、イスラエルのネタニヤフ首相が２７日にＵＡＥを訪問し、ムハンマド大統領と会談したと報じた。

items.title: Jefferies' record equities haul offsets asset management slump
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Jefferies Financial beat third-quarter profit estimates on Monday, as higher fees from advising on deals and underwriting stock sales were complemented by a record haul in equities trading business.
items.body:
Jefferies Financial (JEF.N) beat third-quarter profit estimates on Monday, as higher fees from advising on deals and underwriting stock sales were complemented by a record haul in equities trading business.
Its asset management business, however, took a hit, with fees and investment return revenue shrinking to $34 million from $84 million a year earlier. That reflects weaker performance across several fund strategies, including Point Bonita, which had exposure to bankrupt auto-parts supplier First Brands.
Global dealmaking has crossed $4 trillion this year as corporate boardrooms look past market volatility, taking advantage of an easier regulatory backdrop to scale their businesses.
Jefferies' investment banking revenue jumped 17% to $1.33 billion, underpinned by record advisory business performance and strong equity underwriting.
The New York-based investment bank's results are closely watched on Wall Street for an early glimpse into quarterly investment banking trends, before large US banks report earnings in the coming weeks.
Revenue from capital markets business, which houses Jefferies' trading desks, jumped 11% to $802 million, driven by record equities trading performance.
"We are very optimistic about the balance of 2026 and our momentum heading into 2027, supported by the breadth and strength of our current backlog and new business activity," CEO Richard Handler and President Brian Friedman said.
Handler and Friedman said they remain confident in the long-term outlook for the asset management business as Jefferies continues to reposition the platform.
Profit attributable to Jefferies shareholders was $260.6 million, or $1.08 per share, in the three months ended August 31. Analysts, on average, estimated a profit of $1 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG.
Its shares were down 1.5% in extended trading, and have fallen roughly 24% this year.

items.title: Papa León afirma que preocupaciones sobre el fin del mundo a causa de la IA no son "noticias falsas"
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El papa León afirmó el lunes que los temores de que la inteligencia artificial pueda destruir el mundo no son "noticias falsas" y deben tomarse en serio, en lo que pareció un reproche al presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump.
items.body:
El papa León afirmó el lunes que los temores de que la inteligencia artificial pueda destruir el mundo no son "noticias falsas" y deben tomarse en serio, en lo que pareció un reproche al presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump.
León, que ha advertido de los peligros de la IA a lo largo de sus 16 meses de pontificado, también criticó directamente a los directores ejecutivos del sector que defendían que no debería haber límites para esta tecnología.
"Creo que las preocupaciones planteadas por muchos de los expertos y especialistas en IA deben tomarse en serio", afirmó el pontífice en una rueda de prensa durante su vuelo de regreso a Roma, tras un viaje de cuatro días a Francia. "No creo que se trate de noticias falsas, como algunos han dicho".
Trump declaró ante la Asamblea General de la ONU la semana pasada que, en su opinión, los temores sobre los peligros que la IA supone para la humanidad eran un "engaño".
El papa señaló que había leído el lunes que el director de la empresa fabricante de chips Nvidia había anunciado que podría haber una forma de incorporar medidas de seguridad en ciertos modelos de IA. Sin embargo, se mostró escéptico y añadió: "Pero es el mismo que dice que no debería haber límites ni regulación gubernamental".
El director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, declaró este mes a CBS News que coincidía con Trump en que las preocupaciones sobre la seguridad de la IA eran exageradas.
León instó al mundo a "promover el diálogo, el estudio y la investigación para encontrar formas de garantizar que la IA no llegue a un punto en el que pueda destruir a la humanidad".
"Creo que hay suficientes personas seriamente interesadas en ello (...) pero tenemos que seguir trabajando", afirmó. "No podemos limitarnos a quedarnos de brazos cruzados y fingir que no va a pasar nada".

items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El papa León instó el lunes a Rusia y Ucrania a sentarse a la mesa y debatir cómo poner fin a la guerra, pocas horas después de haber pedido a los líderes europeos que buscan solucionar conflictos a que hagan concesiones para lograr la paz.
items.body:
El papa León instó el lunes a Rusia y Ucrania a sentarse a la mesa y debatir cómo poner fin a la guerra, pocas horas después de haber pedido a los líderes europeos que buscan solucionar conflictos a que hagan concesiones para lograr la paz.
El pontífice también condenó a los líderes nacionales que, según él, "están empezando a hablar de armas nucleares y de guerras cada vez más destructivas", en una rueda de prensa celebrada a bordo de su vuelo de regreso a Roma tras un viaje de cuatro días a Francia.
León afirmó que la Iglesia católica, con 1.400 millones de fieles, tiene la obligación de hacer un llamamiento a la paz y al respeto por la vida humana.
"La Iglesia tiene la responsabilidad de promover estos valores, invitando continuamente a los líderes —tanto de Rusia como de Ucrania, así como de otros países— a reunirse, sentarse a la mesa y entablar un diálogo", destacó.
Añadió que los líderes deben "buscar formas de resolver los problemas sin prolongar estas guerras, que ya no tienen sentido".
"No se trata de ser político o apolítico, sino de que debe haber una voz que busque promover los valores de la dignidad humana, la importancia de la vida y la posibilidad de, tal vez, invertir más en sanidad y educación y menos en armas", sostuvo.
León afirmó el lunes que Europa debe estar dispuesta a sacrificar algunas posiciones para alcanzar la paz, en un discurso pronunciado en Metz, Francia, donde expuso su visión más clara hasta la fecha sobre el futuro del continente.

Sept 28 : Advanced Micro Devices said on Monday it would acquire Fei-Fei Li's AI startup World Labs in an all-stock deal valued at $8.2 billion, giving the chipmaker deeper access to research on AI systems that can understand and simulate the physical world.
The deal gives AMD a foothold in AI-model research as the industry moves beyond chatbots toward systems that can reason about, simulate and interact with the physical world, helping the chipmaker tailor its infrastructure to those emerging workloads.
San Francisco-based World Labs, which raised $1 billion in a funding round earlier this year, develops spatial-intelligence models that can generate, reconstruct and simulate interactive three-dimensional environments from text, image and video inputs.
The technology is aimed at helping AI systems better understand and reason about the physical world, with potential uses in robotics, simulation, design and other real-world applications.

Li, a prominent AI researcher known for her work in computer vision, will join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist after the transaction closes. She will report to CEO Lisa Su. The deal is expected to close by the end of 2026.

items.title: Wall St cai com preços do petróleo e rendimentos do Tesouro em alta
items.author: Chuck Mikolajczak, Johann Cherian
items.creator: Chuck Mikolajczak, Johann Cherian
items.summary: As ações nos EUA caíram nesta segunda-feira, à medida que os preços do petróleo e os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro subiram, com os investidores avaliando a incerteza em relação às perspectivas de um acordo de paz na guerra com o Irã e o impacto sobre a trajetória das taxas do Federal Reserve.
items.body:
As ações nos EUA caíram nesta segunda-feira, à medida que os preços do petróleo e os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro subiram, com os investidores avaliando a incerteza em relação às perspectivas de um acordo de paz na guerra com o Irã e o impacto sobre a trajetória das taxas do Federal Reserve.
Os preços do petróleo bruto haviam disparado depois que o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, rejeitou um acordo de paz proposto pelo Irã, mas recuaram diante das expectativas de que mediadores do Catar realizariam negociações com os dois países para chegar a um possível acordo.
Após recuarem das máximas registradas neste mês, os preços do petróleo aceleraram a alta nos últimos dias, à medida que diminuíram as esperanças de que um acordo de paz pudesse estar no horizonte.
A alta nos preços do petróleo bruto e do diesel alimentou os temores de inflação e elevou os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA, juntamente com comentários de autoridades do Fed indicando que mais aumentos nas taxas de juros podem ser necessários caso as pressões sobre os preços não se moderem após o banco central ter elevado as taxas de juros em 25 pontos-base neste mês.
“O Irã está impulsionando os preços do petróleo, e os preços do petróleo estão impulsionando a inflação, e a inflação está impulsionando as taxas de juros”, disse Jack Ablin, estrategista-chefe de investimentos e sócio fundador da Cresset Capital Management, em Chicago. “Estamos chegando a um ponto em que as taxas de juros parecem bastante atraentes em relação às ações, o que é realmente a primeira vez em quase 20 anos; portanto, isso é algo a que certamente estamos prestando atenção.”
“No momento, não se trata tanto de uma questão de lucros, mas sim de valorização”, disse ele. “Quando você tem uma classe de ativos que vem lutando com uma mão amarrada nas costas há 20 anos, de repente ela passa a parecer bastante competitiva.”
O Índice Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) caiu 0,67%, para 51.481,51 pontos, o S&P 500 (.SPX) perdeu 0,77%, para 7.683,69 pontos, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) recuou 0,92%, para 26.820,38 pontos.
A queda do S&P foi a maior queda percentual diária desde 20 de agosto.
As ações da Boeing (BA.N) despencaram 6,9%, sendo um dos maiores fatores de queda do Dow, depois que a Administração Federal de Aviação dos EUA (FAA) anunciou que adiará a certificação do 737 MAX 10 — há muito atrasada — até que um problema de software recém-divulgado seja resolvido.
Contrariando a tendência geral, as ações da Nvidia (NVDA.O) registraram alta de 1,6% depois que a gigante dos chips anunciou uma autorização de recompra de ações no valor de US$150 bilhões, a maior recompra de ações já realizada por uma empresa.
O Irã anunciou uma proposta de paz na Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, realizada na semana passada em Nova York, afirmando que ela havia sido transmitida aos Estados Unidos por meio de mediadores do Catar. Embora Trump tenha dito no sábado que rejeitou a oferta, ele afirmou ao Axios no domingo que esperava que os negociadores norte-americanos continuassem as conversações nesta semana.
A diretora do Federal Reserve Lisa Cook disse nesta segunda-feira que espera que a pressão inflacionária continue nos próximos meses, decorrente da demanda relacionada à inteligência artificial e dos preços mais altos do petróleo, embora não tenha chegado a afirmar que serão necessários mais aumentos nas taxas de juros.
As expectativas de um aumento da taxa de juros pelo Fed em sua reunião de outubro subiram nos últimos dias, em parte devido a dados econômicos que indicam que a economia vem crescendo a um ritmo sólido. Atualmente, os mercados precificam uma probabilidade de 70,3% de um aumento de pelo menos 25 pontos-base na reunião do banco central no mês que vem, acima dos 57,6% registrados há uma semana e dos 17,7% do mês anterior, de acordo com o CME FedWatch.
Vários dados econômicos importantes serão divulgados esta semana, o que poderá ajudar a definir o rumo da política do Fed, incluindo indicadores sobre a inflação e o mercado de trabalho, culminando no relatório de empregos do governo na sexta-feira.
As ações da Tesla (TSLA.O) caíram 3,9% depois que a corretora J.P. Morgan reduziu seu preço-alvo para o papel, citando entregas fracas no terceiro trimestre.

items.title: US stocks: US market falls as higher oil prices, Treasury yields weigh
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: US stocks declined on concerns over rising oil prices and higher Treasury yields affecting the market. Investors are cautious due to uncertainty surrounding a potential Iran war peace deal negotiations. Federal Reserve officials hinted at possible interest rate hikes if inflation continues to rise significantly. Nvidia shares surged after announcing a record $150 billion share buyback, while Tesla shares dropped after a lowered price target.
items.body: US stocks fell on Monday as oil prices and Treasury yields increased, with investors weighing uncertainty over the prospects for an Iran war peace deal and the impact on the Federal Reserve's rate path.Crude prices had jumped after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal from Iran but pared gains on expectations that Qatari mediators would hold talks with the two countries to find a possible deal.After retreating from highs at the start of the month, oil prices have accelerated higher in recent days as hopes that a peace deal may be on the horizon have diminished.The rising prices of crude and diesel fuel have fanned inflation worries and pushed US Treasury yields higher, along with comments from Fed officials indicating that more rate hikes might be needed if price pressures fail to moderate after the central bank raised interest rates by 25 basis points earlier this month. Iran is driving oil prices, and oil prices are driving inflation, and inflation is driving interest rates, said Jack Ablin, chief investment strategist and founding partner at Cresset Capital Management in Chicago. We're getting to a point now where interest rates are looking pretty attractive relative to equities, which is really the first time in close to 20 years, so that's something that we're certainly paying attention to. It's less of an earnings story right now than it is a valuation story, he said. When you get an asset class that has been fighting with one arm tied behind its back for 20 years, now all of a sudden it's looking pretty competitive. According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 lost 59.00 points, or 0.76%, to end at 7,684.41 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 246.62 points, or 0.91%, to 26,822.09. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 343.78 points, or 0.66%, to 51,484.84.Boeing shares tumbled after Federal Aviation Administration Administrator Bryan Bedford said that software problems with the planemaker's 737 MAX will delay certification of the largest variant, the MAX 10, until the agency is satisfied that we don't have an issue here. Helping to curb declines was a gain in Nvidia shares after the chip giant announced a $150 billion share repurchase authorization, the biggest-ever company share buyback.Iran announced a peace proposal at last week's United Nations General Assembly in New York, saying it had been relayed to the United States through Qatari mediators. While Trump said on Saturday he had rejected the offer, he told Axios on Sunday that he expected US negotiators to continue talks this week.Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said on Monday she expects continued inflationary pressure in coming months stemming from AI-related demand and higher oil prices, though she stopped short of saying more interest rate hikes will be needed.Expectations for a rate hike from the Fed at its October meeting have climbed in recent days, in part due to economic data indicating the economy was growing at a solid pace. Markets are currently pricing in a 70.3% chance for an increase of at least 25 basis points at the central bank's meeting next month, up from 57.6% a week ago and 17.7% a month earlier, according to CME FedWatch.Several key economic releases are due this week, which could help shape the path of Fed policy, including a reading on inflation and the labor market, culminating in Friday's government payrolls report.Tesla shares slumped after brokerage J.P.Morgan lowered its price target on the stock, citing weak deliveries in the third quarter.

items.title: California stiffens punishments for lawyers over payments to clients
items.author: David Thomas
items.creator: David Thomas
items.summary: California is taking a harder line against lawyers who pay people to solicit clients after allegations that a law firm used intermediaries to pay people to submit claims under a $4 billion sexual abuse settlement with Los Angeles County.
items.body:
California is taking a harder line against lawyers who pay people to solicit clients after allegations that a law firm used intermediaries to pay people to submit claims under a $4 billion sexual abuse settlement with Los Angeles County.
Governor Gavin Newsom on Sunday signed AB 2039, which creates new civil penalties for violations of the state's ban on "capping," in which lawyers pay people or businesses to help them recruit clients.
California law already prohibited the practice and barred lawyers from hiring people to solicit clients in places such as hospitals and prisons.
The new law stiffens punishments by imposing a $25,000 civil penalty for each violation and requiring the State Bar of California to seek disbarment of lawyers found to have engaged in the practice rather than resolve cases through settlements.
"The State Bar of California welcomes the enactment of AB 2039 and is committed to fully implementing its provisions," George Cardona, the state bar's chief trial counsel, said in a statement.
A spokesperson for Newsom did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Consumer Attorneys of California, a trade group, backed the legislation.
Assembly member Rick Chavez Zbur, a Democrat who sponsored the legislation and analyses produced by legislative staff, cited reporting by the Los Angeles Times about alleged false claims that were submitted under a $4 billion settlement that the Los Angeles County [USN:L3N3QI1F1 TEXT:"reached last year"] to resolve more than 6,800 sexual abuse claims dating back to 1959.
The Los Angeles Times reported that one plaintiffs law firm, Downtown LA Law Group, represented nine people who said they were allegedly paid to file claims under the sexual abuse settlement, and that some of the claims were false.
DTLA firm did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Monday but has [USN:L6N42C142 TEXT:"previously denied wrongdoing"].
Both the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office and the state bar said they had launched their own investigations into the false claims.

items.title: Café arábica sobe mais de 3% em NY; açúcar bruto se mantém estável
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Os contratos futuros de café arábica na bolsa ICE subiram mais de 3% nesta segunda-feira, em uma recuperação técnica impulsionada pela oferta reduzida dos produtores, enquanto os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto se mantiveram estáveis.
items.body:
Os contratos futuros de café arábica na bolsa ICE subiram mais de 3% nesta segunda-feira, em uma recuperação técnica impulsionada pela oferta reduzida dos produtores, enquanto os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto se mantiveram estáveis.
CAFÉ * Os contratos futuros de café arábica em Nova York fecharam com alta de 10,15 centavos, ou 3,6%, a US$2,8875 por libra-peso, após uma queda de 5,4% na semana passada.
* Corretores afirmaram que o mercado estava maduro para uma correção técnica após uma queda acentuada que se seguiu a um pico no final de agosto, que marcou o preço mais alto desde janeiro.
* "Acho que uma recuperação já estava mais do que na hora, depois da queda que vimos nos últimos 30 dias", disse um corretor de uma empresa europeia de café.
* Ele acrescentou que o salto diário nos preços foi impulsionado pela baixa liquidez, com um interesse de venda tímido por parte de operadores e produtores.
* O arábica, no entanto, continua sob pressão devido às expectativas de que o Brasil tenha colhido uma safra recorde em 2026/27, mas os corretores afirmaram que as crescentes preocupações com a qualidade podem significar que a quantidade real de café disponível para uso comercial seja abaixo do esperado.
* O café robusta subiu 1,3%, para US$3.412 por tonelada métrica.
AÇÚCAR * O açúcar bruto fechou em queda de 0,04 centavo, ou 0,2%, a 17,46 centavos por libra-peso, após ter sido negociado em alta no início do pregão.
* Os preços do petróleo subiram devido às renovadas tensões entre os EUA e o Irã, estimulando usinas de cana a aumentar a produção de etanol, biocombustível à base de cana, em detrimento do açúcar.
* A Suedzucker (SZUG.DE) , maior produtora de açúcar da União Europeia, elevou as expectativas de lucro para a safra 2026/27 devido à maior demanda por biocombustíveis.
* O preço do açúcar tem apresentado tendência de alta nas últimas semanas, já que as chuvas no Brasil prejudicaram a colheita.
* O serviço de monitoramento de safras Mars reduziu, nesta segunda-feira, sua previsão para o rendimento agrícola da beterraba sacarina na União Europeia.
* O preço do açúcar branco subiu 0,3%, para US$504,10 por tonelada.
(Reportagem de May Angel e Marcelo Teixeira)

items.title: Pope Leo says concerns about AI doom scenarios are not 'fake news'
items.author: Joshua McElwee
items.creator: Joshua McElwee
items.summary: Pope Leo on Monday said concerns that artificial intelligence could destroy the world are not "fake news" and should be taken seriously, in an apparent rebuke of US President Donald Trump.
items.body:
Pope Leo on Monday said concerns that artificial intelligence could destroy the world are not "fake news" and should be taken seriously, in an apparent rebuke of US President Donald Trump.
The first US pope, who has warned of the dangers of AI throughout his 16-month papacy, also directly criticized technology CEOs who argued there should be no guardrails on the technology.
"I do think that the concerns raised by many of the experts, specialists in AI, should be taken seriously," the pontiff said in a press conference on his flight back to Rome after a four-day trip to France. "I don't think that that is fake news, as some have said."
Trump told the UN General Assembly last week that he believed fears about the dangers to humanity from AI were a "hoax."
The pope said he had read on Monday that the head of chipmaker Nvidia had announced there could be a way to insert guardrails into certain AI models. But Leo expressed scepticism, adding: "He's the same one, however, that says there should be no limits placed and no government regulation."
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang told CBS News this month that he agreed with Trump that safety concerns about AI were overblown.
Trump is to meet with tech CEOs on artificial intelligence on Tuesday at the White House. Huang, Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Greg Brockman are among those who will meet Trump and House of Representatives Speaker Mike Johnson, according to sources familiar with the matter. Other possible attendees include Google CEO Sundar Pichai and SpaceXAI executive Elon Musk.
Johnson said the talks would focus on [USN:L6N45K0R1 TEXT:"finding a balance"] between innovation and oversight and warned that the US risks losing the AI race to China if it decides to "hyper-regulate this."
Leo urged the world "to promote dialogue, study, investigation, to find ways to make sure that AI does not get to a point where it could destroy humanity."
"I think that there are enough people seriously interested in that … but we have to keep working," said the pope. "We can't just sit back and pretend nothing's going to happen."
items.raw_description: Pope Leo on Monday said concerns that artificial intelligence could destroy the world are not "fake news" and should be taken seriously, in an apparent rebuke of US President Donald Trump.

items.title: Ibovespa tem baixa modesta com exterior desfavorável e eleição indefinida
items.author: Paula Arend Laier
items.creator: Paula Arend Laier
items.summary: O Ibovespa fechou com uma queda modesta nesta segunda-feira, após uma sessão sem um sinal único, em meio a um ambiente externo ainda negativo e novas pesquisas eleitorais, mas contrapeso positivo de Petrobras, com novo avanço do petróleo no exterior.
items.body:
O Ibovespa fechou com uma queda modesta nesta segunda-feira, após uma sessão sem um sinal único, em meio a um ambiente externo ainda negativo e novas pesquisas eleitorais, mas contrapeso positivo de Petrobras, com novo avanço do petróleo no exterior.
Índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) cedeu 0,26%, a 182.991,13 pontos, após alcançar 181.931,36 na mínima e 184.094,65 na máxima. O volume financeiro no pregão somou R$25,46 bilhões.
Na visão do estrategista-chefe da Eleven Financial, Fernando Siqueira, o mercado aqui está sendo muito pautado pelas eleições. "As últimas notícias são meio neutras, não dá para ter uma definição, uma visão clara de quem é o vencedor", afirmou. "A semana vai ser bem volátil."
Pesquisas sobre intenção de votos para a eleição brasileira, que terá o primeiro turno no próximo domingo, seguiram mostrando um cenário acirrado entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) pelo Palácio do Planalto.
Na [USN:S8N442011 TEXT:"BTG/Nexus"], Lula aparece com 42% e o Flávio com 37% no primeiro turno da eleição, enquanto, em um potencial segundo turno entre ambos, o petista tem 46% e o candidato do PL registra 44%, dentro da margem de empate técnico.
A [USN:S0N44O04S TEXT:"Quaest"], divulgada pela GloboNews, mostrou Lula e Flávio empatados com 42% das intenções de voto em um eventual segundo turno, enquanto Lula lidera o primeiro turno com 39% e Flávio soma 34%.
Investidores também repercutiram nesta segunda-feira anúncios realizados pelo governo Lula na última sexta-feira, incluindo a proibição das operações de [USN:L1N45H0WI TEXT:"apostas"] online no país e o [USN:L1N45H0VW TEXT:"Desenrola Brasil 3.0"], um novo programa para ajudar pessoas endividadas.
O analista João Daronco, da Suno Research, afirmou que a semana será bastante ditada pelas pesquisas eleitorais e o cenário externo pode ajudar ou atrapalhar. Nesta sessão, observou, pesou do lado negativo, com a alta do petróleo, que apoia perspectivas piores para inflação, com efeito na curva de juros e na bolsa.
"Se não fosse a Petrobras e as petrolíferas, hoje a bolsa estaria caindo ainda mais", afirmou. O índice Small Caps (.SMLL) , que não tem as ações da Petrobras em sua composição, fechou em queda de 1,2%.
No exterior, o barril do petróleo sob o contrato Brent fechou em alta de 0,92%, a US$105,28, afastando-se das máximas do dia, quando saltou a US$108,83 o barril, em meio ao impasse nas negociações entre Estados Unidos e Irã.
Em um contexto de preocupações com a inflação e os próximos passos do Federal Reserve, os rendimentos dos títulos de 10 anos do Tesouro norte-americano avançavam a 5,2319% no final do dia , de 5,181% na sexta-feira. Em Nova York, o índice acionário S&P 500 (.SPX) fechou em baixa de 0,77%.
DESTAQUES

items.title: Pope urges Russia, Ukraine to sit down and discuss how to end war
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Pope Leo on Monday urged Russia and Ukraine to sit down and discuss how to end their four-year war, hours after he had urged European leaders seeking to end conflicts to make concessions to achieve peace.
items.body:
Pope Leo on Monday urged Russia and Ukraine to sit down and discuss how to end their four-year war, hours after he had urged European leaders seeking to end conflicts to make concessions to achieve peace.
The first US pope also decried national leaders who he said are "beginning to speak about nuclear weapons and wars that are becoming ever more destructive," addressing a press conference aboard his flight to Rome after a four-day trip to France.
Leo said the 1.4-billion-member Catholic Church has an obligation to call for peace and respect of human life.
"The Church has a responsibility to promote these values, continually inviting leaders -- from Russia and Ukraine, as well as other countries -- to come together, sit down, engage in dialogue," said the pope.
He said leaders must "seek ways to solve problems without continuing these wars, which no longer make sense."
"This is not about being political or nonpolitical, but there needs to be a voice that seeks to promote the values of human dignity, the importance of life, and the possibility of perhaps spending more on health and education and less on weapons," said Leo.
Earlier on Monday, the pope said Europe must be willing to sacrifice some positions to achieve peace in a speech in Metz, France, where he laid out his clearest vision yet for the future of the continent.

items.title: Costa Rica despide a argentino "Bocha" Batista como DT de selección tras derrotas en Liga de Naciones Concacaf
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: La Federación Costarricense de Fútbol (FCRF) despidió el lunes al argentino Fernando "Bocha" Batista como director técnico de la selección, un día después de que el representativo centroamericano sufriera su segunda derrota consecutiva en la Liga de Naciones de la Concacaf y quedara al borde de la eliminación.
items.body:
La Federación Costarricense de Fútbol (FCRF) despidió el lunes al argentino Fernando "Bocha" Batista como director técnico de la selección, un día después de que el representativo centroamericano sufriera su segunda derrota consecutiva en la Liga de Naciones de la Concacaf y quedara al borde de la eliminación.
En su lugar, la FCRF nombró como director técnico interino al ex mundialista Bryan Ruiz.
"Fernando Batista y su cuerpo técnico fueron separados de sus puestos al frente de la selección nacional mayor masculina. En su lugar, el ex seleccionado nacional y director técnico Bryan Ruiz asumirá de forma interina la Tricolor para enfrentar los juegos pendientes de Costa Rica en la Nations League de Concacaf", informó la FCRF en un breve comunicado.
Batista, de 56 años, fue designado técnico de Costa Rica en febrero, en sustitución del mexicano Miguel "Piojo" Herrera, quien fue cesado tras no cumplir el objetivo de llevar a la selección "tica" a la Copa del Mundo.
Batista dirigió seis partidos a Costa Rica, y registró un empate y cinco derrotas, siendo la más severa la que sufrió el jueves en la Liga de Naciones de la Concacaf ante Curazao por 4-3, en un partido que iba ganando por tres goles. Y el domingo volvió a perder ante Haití por 2-0.
"Cuando lo contratamos pensamos en todo el proceso para 2030, pero también hay que tomar decisiones sobre la marcha y este es un cambio que se está decidiendo por por los malos resultados en estas dos fechas de la Liga de Naciones”, dijo a periodistas el presidente de la FCRF, Osael Maroto.
"La apuesta que hicimos con Batista no tuvo resultados, pero eso no significa que fuera de nuestras fronteras no haya gente que nos vaya a llevar a los resultados que estamos esperando”, agregó.
El próximo compromiso de Costa Rica será el 1 de octubre cuando visite a Nicaragua en la tercera jornada de la Liga de Naciones de la Concacaf, que otorga boletos para la Copa Oro del 2027.
